metric_identity.metric_name: Stargate Project — $500B US AI infrastructure joint venture by OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle, and MGX
metric_identity.source_report: Official announcement by OpenAI (January 2025); subsequent updates via OpenAI blog posts, CNBC, Bloomberg, Reuters, and Wikipedia tracking of Stargate LLC milestones
metric_identity.publication_date: January 21, 2025 (formal announcement); ongoing updates through February 2026
metric_identity.methodology_notes: Investment figures are based on announced commitments by equity partners (SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, MGX) and reported agreements. Job creation figures are estimates from the venture partners. Power capacity (GW) is based on announced data center site plans and utility agreements. Financial details from The Information, Bloomberg, and Reuters reporting on internal financing structures. Actual deployed capital vs. committed capital differs significantly — initial commitment was $100B with $500B total by 2029.

metric_value.value: Multiple key metrics: (1) Total announced investment: $500B over 4 years (2025-2029); (2) Initial deployment: $100B immediate commitment at launch; (3) Equity structure: SoftBank and OpenAI each committed ~$19B and hold ~40% ownership each; Oracle and MGX each contributed ~$7B; (4) Power capacity target: 10 GW by 2029; current planned capacity exceeds 8 GW with over $450B in investment commitments; (5) Data center sites: Abilene TX (flagship, operational), plus 5 additional sites announced (Shackelford County TX, Dona Ana County NM, Lordstown OH, Milam County TX, and a midwestern US site), plus Michigan campus (construction early 2026); (6) GPU deployment: 16,000 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs at Abilene by summer 2025, target 64,000 by end of 2026; (7) Oracle partnership: 4.5 GW additional capacity, exceeding $300B between the two companies over 5 years; (8) Job creation claims: 100,000+ US jobs (partner estimate); (9) International expansion: Stargate UAE announced — 1 GW data center in Abu Dhabi, 200 MW live in 2026; Argentina partnership with Sur Energy for up to $25B / 500 MW; (10) JPMorgan Chase $2.3B loan for Abilene construction (May 2025)
metric_value.unit: USD (billions), gigawatts (GW), GPU count, job count
metric_value.geographic_scope: US (primary — Texas, New Mexico, Ohio, Michigan, midwestern US); UAE and Argentina (international expansion)
metric_value.comparison_baseline: Prior to Stargate, the largest announced AI infrastructure investment was Microsoft's $80B commitment for AI data centers in FY2025. Google announced $75B in 2025 capex. The $500B Stargate figure dwarfs all prior AI infrastructure commitments by a factor of 5-6x. For context, total US data center market was valued at approximately $60B in 2024.

trend.trend_direction: Accelerating (rapid site expansion and partnership announcements, though financing challenges and scale-backs introduce uncertainty)
trend.year_over_year_change: From zero to $100B committed and flagship site operational within 9 months of announcement (Jan-Sep 2025); planned capacity grew from 1 GW initial to over 8 GW within 12 months; 5 new sites announced within first 8 months; international expansion (UAE, Argentina) initiated within first 10 months
trend.forecast_value: $500B total investment and 10 GW power capacity by 2029; 64,000 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs at Abilene by end of 2026; next-generation NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips expected to come online in 2026; Michigan campus construction beginning early 2026
trend.velocity_indicator: time_to_unicorn: Stargate went from announcement to operational flagship data center in under 9 months; construction to first AI workloads in Abilene took less than one year

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: The Stargate Project represents the most ambitious AI infrastructure bet in history and signals several critical dynamics for founders. First, it demonstrates that the AI infrastructure layer is consolidating around a small number of mega-scale players (OpenAI, SoftBank, Oracle, Microsoft, Google), meaning startups cannot compete on raw compute — they must build on top of this infrastructure. The $500B figure sets the scale expectation for what it takes to be a foundation model provider, effectively raising the barrier to entry for compute-intensive AI companies to sovereign-wealth-fund levels. Second, the project creates massive derivative opportunities: the 100,000+ jobs claim (even if inflated) signals demand for AI-specialized construction, cooling, power generation, and data center management services. Third, the 10 GW power requirement highlights the energy bottleneck in AI scaling — startups in AI-optimized energy (nuclear, geothermal, grid management), cooling technology, and energy-efficient inference hardware have a structural tailwind. Fourth, the financing struggles (SoftBank scrambling for $22.5B, selling Nvidia shares, Mizuho Bank $3B loan) reveal that even $500B ventures face capital constraints — the AI infrastructure build-out may be more fragile than headlines suggest. Fifth, Elon Musk's public criticism ('they don't actually have the money') and reports of scale-backs and internal disagreements between SoftBank and OpenAI highlight execution risk. Sixth, for European/French entrepreneurs specifically, Stargate reinforces the US-China AI infrastructure dominance narrative and strengthens the case for European digital sovereignty investments — Mistral AI and EU-funded alternatives become more strategically relevant as counterweights.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Do not try to compete with Stargate on infrastructure — instead build on it. The project creates a predictable, massive compute substrate that enables startups to focus on application-layer and vertical AI solutions. Monitor the project's actual vs. announced progress: if Stargate delivers even 30% of its commitments, inference costs will drop significantly in 2026-2027, enabling new classes of AI applications that are currently cost-prohibitive. The energy constraints (10 GW = roughly 2-3 nuclear power plants worth of electricity) create opportunities in power optimization, sustainable AI infrastructure, and European alternatives. For fundraising narratives, cite Stargate as evidence that infrastructure investment validates the long-term AI market — investors backing the application layer are riding on $500B+ of infrastructure capex being deployed beneath them.

confidence.cross_reference: OpenAI official announcements (January 2025, July 2025, September 2025); CNBC reporting (January 2025, September 2025); Bloomberg reporting on financing challenges (August 2025, May 2025); Reuters reporting on SoftBank funding (December 2025); The Information reporting on equity structure and internal disagreements; Wikipedia Stargate LLC article (aggregated timeline); IEEE Spectrum analysis; S&P Global Market Intelligence; Oracle fact sheet for congressional briefing; Construction Review Online reporting on scale-backs
confidence.caveats: The $500B figure is a commitment target, not deployed capital — actual capital deployed as of early 2026 is a fraction of this amount. SoftBank's financing has been repeatedly described as precarious (scrambling for $22.5B, selling Nvidia shares, seeking bank loans), raising questions about whether the full commitment will materialize. Elon Musk publicly challenged the funding claims. Bloomberg reported in August 2025 that 'no funds were raised to meet the project's initial $500 billion budget.' Internal disagreements between SoftBank and OpenAI over data center locations and operational decisions have been reported. Job creation figures (100,000+) are partner estimates and likely include temporary construction jobs — Bloomberg reported the Abilene site may yield only ~57 permanent jobs. The venture's structure is complex: SoftBank has financial responsibility, OpenAI has operational responsibility, and the transition from OpenAI nonprofit to for-profit may affect SoftBank's investment commitments. International expansions (UAE, Argentina) were not part of the original US-focused announcement and may represent scope creep or alternative funding strategies. Power capacity plans (10 GW) face significant grid and permitting constraints.
